answer.rationale: A release landed two hours ago and write-path p99 latency has been climbing for 90 minutes, strongly implicating the new build as the cause of the degradation. Memory_b1 records that a prior rollback under an analogous checkout-error spike restored stability cleanly with no customer impact. Memory_b6 supports that staged/canary gating catches regressions early, so re-releasing can be done safely later. At settlement peak, writes are heavy, so any intervention must not lose committed transactions; a rollback to the known-good prior build preserves writes while restoring latency. Add_capacity or route_read_replicas might reduce load but would not address a regression introduced by the release. Regional failover and circuit breakers are not indicated because the degradation is latency-driven and release-correlated, not partner-outage or region-specific. If p99 does not improve within ~15 minutes post-rollback, escalate to add_capacity in the next window.
